as_read: The trial evidence is oncology adjunct work on PSK, PSP or unspecified Yun Zhi preparations, with no abstract giving a dose for a sporocarp extract; the only placebo trial with a named primary outcome (n=15, liver cancer) was null.

quote.text: There was no difference in TTP with use of CV compared to placebo.

proposed_decision_text: All five labels print Coriolus versicolor sporocarp extract 1000 mg, and the label rows carry no claim. This review read abstracts only, and no study read meets the standard of a randomized trial or meta-analysis of the ingredient alone, oral, with a stated dose, population and primary outcome with a direction. A meta-analysis of 13 trials reported a 9% absolute reduction in 5-year mortality with Yun Zhi added to conventional anticancer treatment, but its abstract states no dose and no preparation (22185453). A Cochrane review of seven trials in colorectal cancer, in which the extract was used alongside conventional treatment, found low-certainty evidence of a small five-year survival effect (RR 1.08, 95% CI 1.01 to 1.15) and very low-certainty evidence on adverse events (36445793); it describes the extract as PSK and states no dose in its abstract. A systematic review of PSK and Coriolus versicolor extracts in lung cancer reported that most randomized trials supported a positive impact, with conflicting results for some symptoms and median survival, and called for larger trials (25784670). In the placebo trial in 15 people with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma, the primary endpoint of time to progression did not differ, while quality of life was generally better on Coriolus versicolor (28375640); that abstract states no dose or preparation, and the full text was not open to this review. A placebo trial of polysaccharide peptide in 68 people with advanced non-small cell lung cancer reported better blood counts and immunoglobulins and fewer withdrawals for disease progression, but names no primary outcome or dose and tested an isolated peptide (12814145). A trial in 24 healthy volunteers reported gut microbiome changes with polysaccharide peptide, with no primary outcome or dose in the abstract (25006989). Trials in healthy adults and in people with oral HPV, or alongside COVID-19 vaccination, combined the mushroom with Danshen, Ganoderma lucidum or Fomitopsis officinalis, so they do not test it alone (14996412, 25271984, 41620671). A 2023 systematic review of mushroom supplements in cancer care concluded the evidence is inconclusive for routine use (36995535). The evidence therefore does not support credit for a sporocarp extract at 1000 mg, and it does not show that such a product fails.
stop_list: Fields can't express the difference between a sporocarp extract at 1000 mg and PSK or PSP, the isolated fractions used in most of the trial work.
clinician_items: 36445793: authors could not tell whether adverse events were due to the chemotherapy or to the extract itself; evidence on adverse events was very low certainty.

36995535: most mushroom supplement studies reported adverse effects of grade 2 or lower, mainly nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and muscle pain; this review pools 12 mushroom preparations and isn't specific to Coriolus versicolor.
stored_rating_note: Stored positive_moderate rests on one meta-analysis (22185453) of cancer survival with conventional treatment, whose abstract names no dose or preparation. Its 'strong evidence' wording sits beside a later Cochrane colorectal review that grades the survival effect low certainty (36445793). The record's own applicability text already says this doesn't establish general immune support or a dose. Moderate describes oncology adjunct use, not the 1000 mg sporocarp extract on these labels.
unread_notes: Abstracts only. Two searches: 24 hits and 37 hits, titles screened. The PubMed records for 28375640, 12814145 and 25006989 show no PMC id, so their full texts weren't opened; the dose and preparation in 28375640 would come from its full text, and a stated dose could make it a null trial for Coriolus versicolor (n=15). Abstracts of 14996412 and 41620671 were read to 1300 characters, enough to establish that each is a combination; their results aren't described here beyond that. Hits seen by title and not opened: 21087484, 35450034, 33424591, 31030754, 38697129. Vaginal gel papers (33746195, 28302110, 41797457, 41507892) are topical and weren't used. The PMC lookup used a one-line PubMed efetch on PMIDs only, because pm.py doesn't print the PMC id.
